Product brief

Pipeup

Pipe up, right where the work is.

Product skillWrite or update the brief, asking for every missing fact; regenerate and review the documents; build the shared folder.

Problem

People share work as standalone HTML files: reports, specs, prototypes and slide decks, many of them written by AI agents. Those files have no good way to collect feedback. Reviewers reply in chat threads that lose the context of what they were looking at, and the author (or the agent working for them) has to guess where each remark belongs.

Audience

  • MLMaya Lindqvistsomeone sent them an HTML file; they want to say what they think about a sentence, a block or a spot, and hand it back, with no account to make.
  • TATom Adeyemithey made the page (or an agent did), add one line to it, and want every comment pinned to the exact place so an agent can act on it.

Value

Pipeup turns any HTML page into a reviewable document with one script tag. Reviewers select words, click a block or drop a pin and comment in place. Comments stay in their own browser, and Copy comments as Markdown turns them into text that says exactly where each comment is, ready to send to the author or paste into an AI agent.

What sets it apart

  • No accounts and no servers: Pipeup itself never sends anything anywhere, and a page opened from disk works.
  • The page stays the author's: nothing is restyled, moved or covered, and outside comment mode the page behaves exactly as before.
  • Comments carry their place: the slide or section, the element, the quoted words or the pin, so an agent knows where to act.
  • One set of gestures covers text, blocks, pins and the page as a whole.
  • Add-ons, each chosen by the author or turned on by the reviewer, add what plain Pipeup leaves out: Emoji, Voice, Share, Live, Save to GitHub, My identity, Inbox, Updates, Inline asks and Agents. Their rows sit in Pipeup's menu.
  • Pipeup for browsers, the extension for Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, adds the same Pipeup to any page from the toolbar; nothing is added until the reviewer asks.

Not for

  • Reviewing images or PDFs on their own.
  • A hosted service, accounts, dashboards or notifications: sharing and live review are optional add-ons the author chooses.
  • Rich comments: formatting, images or embedded content. Comments are plain text with line breaks and links.
  • Replacing the chat or tracker where decisions are made; Pipeup collects the feedback and hands it on.

Platform

  • Runs on: current desktop and mobile browsers, on any HTML page opened from disk, served locally or hosted on the web.
  • Appearance: the light theme by default; the person can switch to dark or automatic from the comment control's menu, and the choice is remembered for that page in that browser.
  • Sizes: phones from 390 px wide upward; on wide windows the comment column sits beside the content, and on narrow screens threads open below what they are about and All comments takes the full width.
  • Input: pointer (one click on the control starts and stops commenting; ⋯ beside it opens the menu), keyboard (Shift+Alt+C, ⇧⌥C on a Mac, toggles comment mode; Esc steps out) and touch (one tap; press and hold for the menu). Selecting words offers a comment in comment mode and out of it.
  • Start and stop: the page opens with its comments showing and comment mode off; comments, the person's name and the hidden choice are kept in that browser for that page.

Success criteria

SC-001
A reviewer with no account comments on a sentence within a minute of opening the page. Measure: Open question How will this be observed: moderated sessions, or something counted?
SC-002
An author pastes copied comments into a coding agent and the agent finds every place without asking. Measure: Open question How many pastes, and who judges that the agent found the place?

For investors

What the Pitch tells investors: the future it bets on, then the facts. Nothing here is invented: an open part is a clarification marker until someone who knows says.

Vision

Open question What future will play out, in one sentence, that makes this product necessary?

Why now

Generative AI is producing more content than ever, and much of it is HTML: websites, reports and presentations. Anthropic and OpenAI host what their tools make, but each locks it to its own platform. There is room for one consistent way to share and review it that works for everyone, adopted the way WordPress was: so easy to use that it simply gets adopted.

MeasureValueSourceDate
New English web pages with some AI-written content74.2%Ahrefs2025-05-19
Websites built on WordPress38.3%W3Techs2026-11-27
Sites with a known CMS that use WordPress57.3%W3Techs2026-11-27
ChatGPT weekly users900MTechCrunch2026-02-27

Each vendor keeps what its tool makes on its own platform: shared Claude artifacts are hosted on claude.site (simonwillison.net, 2024-07-09), artifacts from Claude Code cannot be made public outside the organisation (Anthropic, 2026-06-18), and ChatGPT shares live under chatgpt.com/share (OpenAI Help). Ahrefs' 74.2% counts any AI involvement, not pages written mostly by AI (ahrefs.com/blog/what-percentage-of-new-content-is-ai-generated); W3Techs' shares change daily (w3techs.com/technologies/details/cm-wordpress); ChatGPT's 900M weekly users (techcrunch.com/2026/02/27/chatgpt-reaches-900m-weekly-active-users).

Formats became universal once they were open: Markdown in 2004 (daringfireball.net); OpenDocument as ISO/IEC 26300 in 2006; PDF as ISO 32000-1 in 2008, with Adobe's royalty-free licence; Office Open XML as ISO/IEC 29500 in 2008; HTML5 as a W3C Recommendation in 2014. WordPress spread the same way: open source (GPL) since 2003 and built for minimal setup (wordpress.org/about).

The gap

People still want to work together on what gets made. Getting feedback matters, and making it easy is crucial.

The bridge

Pipeup gives AI agents a flexible way to see which parts of the content are being discussed and need changes. With an optional backend and a simple API, it adapts to any agent's use, such as asking for comments in place on the page.

Market

Most developers now work with AI tools, and a third already use AI agents, so feedback has to reach an agent, not only a person.

Sources: survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/ai and the survey's press release (stackoverflow.co/company/press).

Competition

Google Docs and Microsoft Office set what people expect from comments: select the words, comment in place, reply and resolve. Pipeup makes that everyday experience available to everyone who creates HTML content, with no account and no server. The newer commenting tools hand comments to AI agents, but each needs an account, a hosted service or a local server, or works only in its own setup; none is one script tag that works on any HTML file.
